topic: Frugal Tokens: Tracking Cost and Usage Across Coding Agents
summary: Frugal Tokens (dpclark4/frugal-tokens, Show HN 2026-08-19, 37 pts) is a local-only Deno dashboard that reads the session transcripts coding agents already write to disk (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, PI, Cursor) and turns them into spend, working-time and cache-miss analytics. Its distinguishing premise is not 'how much did I spend' but 'why did I spend it' - it classifies cache misses (TTL expiry, first-write, truncation) and prices them in dollars. The category is now crowded and asymmetric: ccusage (~18.8k stars, npm-first, 18 sources) owns the CI/statusline niche, AgentsView (~6.0k stars, Go, 60+ agent formats) owns the searchable-archive niche, and Frugal Tokens competes on a single differentiated axis - cache-miss attribution - while being the smallest of the serious entrants (~25 stars) and shipping with no license file. For practitioners the durable lesson is that agent spend is a context-lifecycle problem, not a per-token price problem: vendor head-to-head benchmarks show the same frontier model costing 23-33% less purely from retrieval and context hygiene, and enterprise control is moving into first-party OpenTelemetry (claude_code.cost.usage / claude_code.token.usage) rather than third-party scrapers.

competitors.name: Frugal Tokens (subject)
key_points: Local, read-only view of token usage and reported cost across OpenCode, Claude Code, PI, Codex and Cursor sessions (README).
Requires Deno 2.9+; one-command setup (deno task build && deno task start), serves on http://localhost:9000.
Deeper than competitors on cache economics: classifies miss types and their monetary cost - author cites a single TTL miss after idling ~90 minutes costing $6 for one message.
Session explorer drills to individual model calls, tool inputs/outputs, and 'jump to the cache miss'.
Cost-comparison view re-prices a recorded session under another model's rates, including Anthropic 5m vs 1h caching.
Repo created 2026-07-10, last pushed 2026-09-28, 25 stars / 5 forks, NO license file, no repo description.

competitors.name: ccusage
key_points: The category default: 18,811 stars / 856 forks, created 2025-05-29, pushed 2026-09-30, license NOASSERTION.
Positioned as an analysis CLI for coding agent CLI token usage from local data, run via npx/bunx/nix.

Broadest harness coverage of the CLI-first tools: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Amp, Droid, Codebuff, Hermes Agent, pi-agent, Goose, OpenClaw, Kilo, Kimi, Qwen, GitHub Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Grok Build CLI, ZCode - 18 named sources.
Reports by daily/weekly/monthly/session, plus Claude Code 5-hour billing-window blocks and a statusline hook (beta); JSON output and --by-agent for automation.
Monetization/ops signal: README carries a sponsored team/enterprise slot (Lineman.io) pitching 40% lower token usage and unauthorized-spend alerts - i.e. the pain point is now procurement-level.

competitors.name: AgentsView (kenn-io/agentsview)
key_points: Local-first searchable archive of coding sessions: 6,032 stars / 683 forks, created 2026-02-19, pushed 2026-09-30, MIT, Go single binary.

Parses 60+ agent formats (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Copilot, Windsurf, Zed, Aider, OpenHands, ZCode, OpenClaw, Cline CLI, Kimi, Qwen, Hermes and more) into a SQLite 'archive of record'; optional PostgreSQL/DuckDB/ClickHouse.

Activity dashboard: peak concurrency and the exact moment it happened, active vs idle time, agent-minutes across parallel sessions, cost; filterable by project, agent and machine; live sync while sessions run.
Explicitly surfaces cached vs not-cached tokens (per maintainer reply in the Frugal Tokens HN thread) - it entered the cache-visibility lane too.
Marketed as staying on the machine unless a feature that shares it is turned on; desktop, web, CLI and MCP surfaces.

competitors.name: Agentic Metric
key_points: Show HN 'top for your AI coding agents (token, cost tracking)'; 200 stars / 14 forks, Python, MIT, created 2026-03-04, last pushed 2026-03-09 - abandoned-looking.
Local-only monitoring tool for AI coding agents; the thin end of the long tail of single-author trackers.

competitors.name: Vigilo
key_points: Rust local audit trail and cost tracker for AI coding agents; MIT; 4 stars, created 2026-02-18, last pushed 2026-02-25.
Frames the problem as audit rather than optimization: 'see exactly what Claude Code and Cursor read, wrote, and executed - locally, in real time', with an MCP server surface.
Illustrates how many entrants converge on the same local-transcript-parse architecture; most never reach adoption.

competitors.name: Augment Code - 'Opus 4.7 for 33% less' (vendor benchmark, 2026-05-15, updated 2026-06-18)
key_points: Vendor head-to-head of Auggie CLI vs Claude Code on the same model (Opus 4.7), so the delta is harness/retrieval, not model price.
Terminal Bench 2.0: pass rate 67.4% vs 66.3% (1.1% gap, inside run variance) at 33% lower spend - $463.04 vs $694.50.
SWE-Bench Pro: 1,651,716,301 vs 2,349,143,356 total tokens (-30%), $1,448.63 vs $1,869.97 (-23%), pass rate slightly ahead.
Framing to quote carefully: 'token spend is now a board-level line item'; vendor claims up to 50% savings with its Prism model routing - treat as vendor-supplied.

stats.fact: Anthropic cache pricing multipliers: 5-minute cache write = 1.25x base input; 1-hour cache write = 2x base input; cache hit (read) = 0.1x base input. Caching therefore pays off after one read at 5m TTL, but only after two reads at 1h TTL.
Cache-hit pricing is model-dependent and can be far cheaper than 0.1x: 0.025x on Claude Fable 5.1 / Claude Mythos 5.1 ($0.25/MTok) and 0.05x on Claude Opus 5.5 ($0.20/MTok).

Claude Code emits cost and token telemetry natively via OpenTelemetry: claude_code.cost.usage (USD) and claude_code.token.usage (tokens), alongside session/lines-of-code/commit/PR counters - enabled with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 and an OTLP exporter.

Claude Code deliberately ignores OpenTelemetry exporter variables set in a repository's .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json, so a repo cannot turn telemetry on, redirect it, or capture its own spend data; admins configure it via managed settings instead.

Claude Code can export distributed traces (beta) with span hierarchy and span attributes, and can log raw API request/response bodies behind OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES - which includes the entire conversation history and implies consent to everything the prompt/tool-content gates would reveal.

Same model, same benchmark, different harness: Auggie CLI ran Opus 4.7 on Terminal Bench 2.0 for $463.04 vs Claude Code's $694.50 (-33%), on 32% fewer total tokens and 37% fewer output tokens, with a 1.1% pass-rate gap inside run variance.

Cache reads - not output tokens - dominate agentic spend volume: 341,980,440 of 367,587,892 total tokens (93%) were cache-read tokens in the Auggie Terminal Bench 2.0 run; Claude Code's were 506,455,124 of 543,090,485 (93%).
On SWE-Bench Pro, the same comparison held at 1,651,716,301 vs 2,349,143,356 total tokens (-30%) and $1,448.63 vs $1,869.97 (-23%), with Auggie slightly ahead on pass rate.

Frugal Tokens' author reports a single TTL cache miss - replying ~90 minutes after the previous message - costing $6 for one message, which is the concrete economic argument for cache-miss classification rather than aggregate spend reporting.
Frugal Tokens launched 2026-08-19 with 37 points and 10 comments; repo dpclark4/frugal-tokens created 2026-07-10, last pushed 2026-09-28, 25 stars, 5 forks, no license file.
ccusage is the incumbent by adoption: ccusage/ccusage has 18,811 stars and 856 forks (created 2025-05-29, pushed 2026-09-30) and parses 18 named sources including Hermes Agent, ZCode and OpenClaw.

AgentsView has 6,032 stars / 683 forks (MIT, Go, created 2026-02-19, pushed 2026-09-30) and imports 60+ agent formats into a local SQLite archive with an activity/concurrency dashboard and cost views.
The long tail is mostly dead on arrival: Vigilo (Rust, MIT) has 4 stars with last push 2026-02-25; Agentic Metric (Python, MIT) has 200 stars with last push 2026-03-09.

Practitioner cost-control threads converge on the same levers: model routing, fresh/atomic context threads instead of one long session, compaction via cheaper models, sub-agent briefs as artifacts, and hard iteration/retry caps - 'agents retrying when they shouldn't' is named as the failure mode that visibility alone does not fix.
stats.source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47559293 (Ask HN: How are you keeping AI coding agents from burning money?)

angles: Cache misses, not token prices, are where agent budgets die: a $6 single-message TTL miss is invisible in every spend dashboard that only totals tokens.
The same model can cost 23-33% less purely from harness and retrieval quality - so 'which model' is the wrong first question; 'what does your context lifecycle look like' is the right one.
93% of agentic tokens are cache reads: optimizing input prompts is low-leverage compared to keeping the cache warm and stopping cache-write churn.

Local-first is now table stakes and also the category's ceiling: every serious tool parses the same local JSONL transcripts, so differentiation has moved to interpretation (miss types, concurrency, audit) rather than collection.

Native OpenTelemetry is absorbing the enterprise use case: claude_code.cost.usage and claude_code.token.usage make third-party CLIs redundant for fleet reporting, and repository-level settings are deliberately blocked from redirecting telemetry.

Trust and governance angle: Frugal Tokens ships with no license file while its competitors are MIT/NOASSERTION - a real adoption blocker for anyone running it against corporate session data, and a legitimate caution given agents' transcripts contain source code.
Idle time is a billing event: overlapping sessions, working-time estimates and 'you stepped away for an hour' are cost signals, not just productivity metrics.
The market is consolidating fast - two tools above 6k stars, a graveyard below 200 - so evaluate by data coverage and maintenance, not by feature screenshots.
